purpose: Explain how the NASA Exoplanet Archive chooses a default parameter set and how its composite table mixes references. Rule: for derived quantities, the default parameter set governs; composite values are a counterfactual only, never the answer. This Knowledge Base explains rules, not planet values.

sources.name: Default parameter set and composite row per planet (one dataset source; Context allows one source per dataset)
sources.query: *[(_type == "parameterSet" && defaultFlag == true) || _type == "planet"]{_id, ...select(_type == "parameterSet" => {"title": planet->name + " — default parameter set", "name": planet->name, "planet": planet->name, "source": "NASA Exoplanet Archive default parameter set (one paper, self-consistent)", "paper": publication->citation, "massEarth": massEarth.value, "massKind": massKind, "radiusEarth": radiusEarth.value, "semiMajorAxisAu": semiMajorAxisAu.value}, {"title": name + " — composite table", "name": name, "planet": name, "source": "NASA Exoplanet Archive composite table (values may come from different papers)", "massEarth": compositeSnapshot.massEarth.measurement.value, "massKind": compositeSnapshot.massKind, "massPaper": compositeSnapshot.massEarth.referenceText, "radiusEarth": compositeSnapshot.radiusEarth.measurement.value, "radiusPaper": compositeSnapshot.radiusEarth.referenceText, "semiMajorAxisAu": compositeSnapshot.semiMajorAxisAu.measurement.value, "semiMajorAxisPaper": compositeSnapshot.semiMajorAxisAu.referenceText})}
